title: Surface area of cylinders
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:56Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, mat-surface-area, covers surface area in general, with cylinders only as one bullet and questions on boxes and cubes, so it is broader than this point's cylinder formula and is pitched at Year 11 rather than Year 9.

draft.title: Surface area of cylinders
card: A closed cylinder has 2 circles, one at the top and one at the bottom, and one curved surface around the side.
The two circles each have area πr². Together they give 2πr².
The curved surface unrolls into a rectangle. Its width is the circle's circumference, 2πr, and its height is h. Its area is 2πrh.
SA = 2πr² + 2πrh. Example: r = 2 cm and h = 5 cm. SA = 2π × 4 + 2π × 2 × 5 = 8π + 20π = 28π, which is about 88 cm².
draft.remember: Add the two circles to the unrolled rectangle.

a.q: A closed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. What is its surface area, in terms of π?
a.why: The circles give 2π × 9 = 18π. The curved part gives 2π × 3 × 4 = 24π. The total is 42π cm². 24π is only the curved part, so it leaves out the two circles.
a.clue: Find the circles and the curved part separately.

b.q: A closed tin has diameter 10 cm and height 8 cm. What is its surface area, to the nearest square centimetre?
b.why: The radius is 5 cm. The circles give 2π × 25 = 50π and the side gives 2π × 5 × 8 = 80π. The total is 130π, about 408 cm². Using 10 as the radius gives a much larger wrong answer.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: 18π + 24π = 42π, and 50π + 80π = 130π, which is about 408 cm².
